p01.why: twice is in namespace n and needs qualification from outside, and an int argument adds no namespace to the search.

p02.why: a is out of scope after its block ends, so the use in return is not valid.

p03.why: a is visible after its declaration, so b is 2 and main returns 0.

p04.why: Each inner x hides the outer one for the rest of its scope, so the inner block sees 3 and main's body sees 2.

p05.why: The label is visible in the whole function, also before its definition, so goto skips i = 1 and i stays 0.

p06.why: The unqualified call looks in namespace geo because the argument has type geo::P, so it finds geo::twice and gets 6.

p07.why: The parameter v hides the global v, so f returns 7.

p08.why: a is declared twice in one scope.

p09.why: a is used before its declaration.

p10.why: The body of get sees only names declared before get, and later is declared after it.

p11.why: A variable and a function with one name in one scope are not valid.

p12.why: a is in scope in its own initializer, so the program is valid, but reading a before it has a value is undefined (OBJ-2); best guess is that it returns 0 because the value is never used.

p13.why: A function declared in namespace n can be defined outside it with the qualified name n::f, and the call returns 4.

p14.why: A member declaration sees only earlier members, so T is not declared where t uses it.

p15.why: A label and a variable can share a name, so goto done jumps to the label and main returns the variable, which is 0.

p16.why: ::x reaches the global x through the local one, so the values are 1 and 2.

p17.why: One function must not define the label a twice.

p18.why: The local int f hides the function f, so f() tries to call an int, which is not valid.

p19.why: Ordinary lookup finds ::size and argument lookup adds geo::size, and the argument types pick the right one in each call.

p20.why: The outermost block of a function shares one scope with its parameters, so redeclaring a there is not valid.

p21.why: a is in namespace n, and from outside it needs qualification.

p22.why: g is declared before get, so the body of get sees it and returns 5.

p23.why: Outside the class, a static member needs the class name as qualification, so plain n is not found.

p24.why: The reopened namespace sees a from the earlier part, so n::b is 2.

p25.why: Several declarations of one function are allowed in one scope; there is no main, so the program is not run.

p26.why: A member function body sees members declared after it, so get returns 9.
